3d519529 · 9 files
HeldTurnSink wraps the turn taker's Live sink: when armed, a tapped or woken conversation's first turn (manual activity only) is buffered, Vosk (already in the APK) reads it against the command vocabulary, and the matcher decides. A hit runs the same tool through LiveToolbox.dispatch, says the tool's own words with on-device speech and ends the conversation: Live ran no generation. A miss replays the held turn to Live start to end, so Kevin never repeats himself. Behind Settings key local_commands, OFF until it has run on the phone. Phase 2 of the voice cost work (Kevin: "we offload as much as we can to the phones own speech recognizer"). Timers, alarms, pause/resume/next/previous, volume, dismissal, opening a named screen and clearing ticked lines on a named list. It reads words, not templates (fillers and the companion's name ignored, number words are numbers), walks the tokens once (no regex over the utterance), and misses on anything unaccounted for, anything ambiguous (an alarm with no half of the day), an unknown word or low confidence. LocalCommandPlan maps each command to the same tool call Alfred makes (ADR 0035). Tool diet (F1): service/tools/LiveSurface.kt folds the 93 top-level declarations into 24: 12 direct, 10 action tools whose action values are the old tool names, and two routers (ask: NON_BLOCKING domains; look_up: blocking). Live context rides the system instruction. tools/render_listen_cues.py renders clips with a pluggable renderer. Usage (F7): a LIVE_AUDIT usage line per usageMetadata (counts by modality, thoughts); Live usage is max-folded within a generation and summed across them (it kept the MAX of the whole socket). Crash records 2026-11-10: a SIGSEGV in wake-two-stage at a keyword hit (freed memory) and an uncaught IllegalStateException from startRecording on an uninitialized AudioRecord. Both were beginListening and releaseSpeechService racing on different threads: a release mid-open closed the new Vosk recognizer, or released the new record between its state check and startRecording. WakeCaptureGate serialises open and teardown, runs each chunk's native work only while its capture is open, and a teardown takes the objects out of the fields before freeing them. A capture that will not open gives the mic back and the watchdog backs off instead of throwing. fix(claude-session): warm builds for worker tasks, through the laptop's Gradle lock
alfred-builds 08
53e6b028 · 11 files
Task 7's first compile in a fresh per-task worktree took 23 min 56 s of its 30 minute cap. Three causes: a new worktree with no build outputs, `gradlew --stop` after every build_lock run (so every task started a cold daemon), and nothing shared between tasks. - warm_worktree.py: one persistent worktree, work\warm\wt. `claim --task N --branch B` resets it to the base (checkout -f -B, clean -fd, anything left uncommitted stashed first) and keeps the ignored build outputs, so the next compile is incremental. One task holds it at a time (a lease in the worker root, which helpers cannot write); a needs_confirmation task keeps it up to 6 h for the follow-up that ships it, which inherits it; the worker releases it when a task finishes any other way. Busy: exit 3 and the helper uses a fresh worktree as before. `prepare` seeds it with one compile. - ship.py run on the warm tree takes the lease first and refuses in words if another task holds it, so a ship never checks out a branch under another task's helper. - build_lock.py: never `--stop` (Kevin's laptop rule; the stable private registry keeps the daemon for the next task until Gradle's idle timeout); every Gradle step adds `--max-workers=1 --build-cache` and also takes the laptop's shared mkdir lock (config `gradle_lock`, default the lock g.sh uses), so worker builds and every other agent's Gradle run one at a time. A lock a killed worker build left is cleared once its pid is gone; anyone else's is only waited for. JAVA_HOME falls back to Android Studio's JBR like ship.py. - Prompt rule 12 tells helpers both: claim the warm worktree, and Gradle only via build_lock (shared lock, one worker, never --stop, a long build is waited for, not worked around). Measured 2026-11-09 under the shared lock, --max-workers=1, in task 7's already-built worktree: compileDebugKotlin with a cold daemon 18 s, with a warm daemon 2 s; compiling the unit tests and running the Snake tests 5 min 16 s (25 of 25 pass). Configuration cache stored and reused cleanly there but is left off until assembleFast is checked with it. fix(claude-session): a helper paused on its own build has not ended
no ticket
4414be55 · 4 files
Task 7 (2026-11-06) failed with "The helper stopped without reporting a result" 60 s after the CLI's `completed` notification for a helper that had only parked on its own background compile; its real report 13 minutes later was dropped as "not running". Measured on CLI 2.1.319 (2026-11-09 probe): the raw stream-json task_notification is the same for a pause and for the end (no interim flag; `summary` is the helper's own text). What differs is live children: their task_started carries parent_task_id/owned_by_subagent, and background_tasks_changed lists them. So: - `completed` is recorded, then judged after settle_s: live background work owned by the helper (any depth) means paused, and only the 30 minute cap applies; none means ended. - A helper's task_started again (the CLI resuming it) clears the end state. A child's task_started never replaces the helper, even when its description names the task. - Ended with no report: after report_grace_s the main window gets one `[report N]` reminder to run report.py from the helper's last result; still nothing after another grace, the task fails in words. killed/failed keep the 60 s grace. - A report that arrives after the worker failed the task replaces the failure while it is still in the outbox; once delivered it is kept in reports/late (the engine's FinishView refuses a second finish with 409), never silently dropped. fake_claude.py emits the 2.1.319 shapes (pause, children, background_tasks_changed, resume) and answers reminders; tests cover pause-not-failed, question after a pause, cap while paused, reminder answered, reminder unanswered, and both late-report paths. It now deletes only versions the caller can see. remember with supersedes refuses unless the older memory is about the caller, so no one retires another member's shared fact. Tests for both, a parity test that the read-through list covers LiveToolbox.EPISODIC_EXCLUDED_TOOLS, and the docs corpus regenerated for ADRs 0075 and 0076. Memory v2 (ADR 0075): public.member_memories, private to the member it is about unless shared, read through visible(); REST at /api/member-memories/ (list, create, patch, hard delete with the superseded chain, recall, one-time import) and manage.py import_legacy_memories. Lexical recall with durable (0.999/h) and episodic (0.99/h) decay. A deterministic filter keeps vault identifiers out of memory at every door. Tools: recall_memory, list_memories, remember, forget_memory on /mcp and the web assistant; recruiters excluded; the web prompt says it remembers. This amends engine-mcp ticket 06's memory exclusion for v2 by Kevin's ruling; the legacy tables stay out of the record tools. Worker fence: each heartbeat binds its device token to the Claude machine; memory refuses a listed machine's token and an unbound claude-session token. Consolidation: manage.py consolidate_memories reads finished conversation records (the person's words, tool-free replies only, never a read-through turn), asks the household's model for at most five items, supersedes contradicted facts. Crontab line added, not installed. ID vault (ADR 0076): public.vault_items sealed under LEGION_VAULT_KEY and public.vault_reveals; list/create/update never answer with a value; reveal and delete need a device token, reveal the phone's fingerprint header, 10 an hour, audited without the value. Refused to Claude worker tokens and recruiters. No admin, no tool. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AdhBqkC6Y11DFxD6REwj2o
